item.title: Santa Rosa Winter Lights at Old Courthouse Square — Fri Nov 27, 4:00 PM — Santa Rosa
item.description:
Santa Rosa Metro Chamber’s Winter Lights Tree Lighting Celebration brings holiday magic to Downtown Santa Rosa at Courthouse Square. This free community event features festive family activities, live entertainment, seasonal food and drinks, photos with Santa, and the lighting of the city’s holiday tree. A beloved local tradition for more than 40 years, Winter Lights offers a festive way for families and friends to kick off the holiday season together.
Source: Sonoma.com

item.title: Winter Lights Tree Lighting Celebration — Fri Nov 27, 4:00 PM — Santa Rosa
item.description:

Held at Courthouse Square, this free community event kicks off the holiday season with live entertainment, festive food and drinks, family-friendly activities, photos with Santa and the official lighting of the city’s holiday tree. With more than 40 years of bringing the community together, Winter Lights offers a magical way for families and friends to celebrate the start of the season. Additional details about this year’s celebration will be announced soon.

item.description:

The Harvest Market is a great place to pick up produce, flowers, and eggs harvested from our 6.1 acre sustainable garden. We will be selling products such as fresh produce, eggs from free-range chickens, honey, and olive oil. The market now accepts credit cards. Remember to bring your reusable shopping bag!

item.title: Marin Farmers Markets — Thu Dec 3, 8:00 AM — Marin Veterans' Memorial Auditorium
item.description:
Price: Free
Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market.
Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. The market takes place rain or shine.
www.aginstitutemarin.org
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Dem

item.title: A Celtic Christmas at Luther Burbank Center — Thu Dec 3, 7:30 PM — 50 Mark West Springs Rd
item.description:
Direct from New York’s Off-Broadway and London’s West End, Pace Live presents A Celtic Christmas by A Taste of Ireland at the Luther Burbank Center for the Arts. This holiday spectacular brings the spirit of Christmas to life through melodic folk mash-ups, acapella tap battles, and heartwarming storytelling. Featuring former World Irish Dance Champions and stars from Lord of the Dance and Riverdance, this powerhouse performance blends electrifying rhythms with world-class talent. Audiences will enjoy an evening packed with traditional tunes, heartfelt ballads, Irish wit, and classic holiday carols. It is an unforgettable celebration brimming with energy, charm, and festive magic for the entire family.
Source: Sonoma.com

item.title: Frank Lloyd Wright Civic Center Tours — Fri Dec 4, 10:30 AM — Civic Center
item.description:
Price: Adult $10, Senior/Full Time Student $5 \(Plus a $2 p er ticket service Charge Online\)
Ticket Info:
Sponsor: Marin Center
Link: http://www.marincounty.org/depts/cu
The Frank Lloyd Wright-designed Marin County Civic Center is a national- and state-designated historic landmark. Ninety minute docent-led tours of the Civic Center are offered every Wednesday and Friday at 10:30 am, leaving from the second floor Café, Room 233. The cost is $10 adults and $5 seniors and students. No reservations are required. Groups of ten or more can arrange a private docent tour by calling the Visitor Services Office at \(415\) 473-3762.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.description:

Bank of America, Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank credit and debit cardholders at the Napa Valley Museum of Art and Culture. All you need is your Bank of America, Merrill, or Bank of America Private Bank card and picture ID for access.
Bank of America believes the arts have a unique ability to connect people and communities and help local economies thrive. Through Museums on Us, Bank of America provides its cardholders with free access during the first full weekend of every month to artistic and cultural experiences in California at celebrated institutions ranging from art, children’s and history museums to aquariums, botanical gardens, and science centers.

item.title: Petaluma Children's Business Fair — Sat Dec 5, 11:00 AM — The Spring Hill School
item.description:
Come support the next generation of entrepreneurs at the Children’s Business Fair!
Young entrepreneurs from across Sonoma and Marin Counties will bring their business ideas to life, creating products, developing their brands, setting prices, and selling directly to customers at this one-day marketplace.
More than a market, the fair is a hands-on learning experience designed to build creativity, confidence, financial literacy, and real-world business skills. Throughout the day, local business leaders and entrepreneurs will visit student booths, offering encouragement, practical advice, and feedback to help kids think and grow like business owners.
Come shop, discover unique kid-created products, and support the next generation of local entrepreneurs!
Interested in launching your own business? Children from throughout Sonoma and Marin Counties are invited to participate.

item.title: Petaluma Women’s Chorus Winter 2026 Concert — Sun Dec 6, 4:00 PM — Hall of the Above
item.description:
Our very own Petaluma Women’s Chorus presents the shimmering sounds of snowy nights and winter twilight in their “Winter’s Night” concert at 4 pm on Sunday, December 6, in downtown Petaluma.
The concert features Leo Delibes’ lovely Messe Breve and the spirited “Boa Noite, Minha Gente,” a festive Brazilian song for women inspired by the “baiana” celebration.
This is the Chorus’ first season singing in our new home, the historic Hall of the Above at 199 N. Petaluma Blvd. (the corner of East Washington and Petaluma Boulevard). We can’t wait for you to hear the sound of the full choir performing in the great acoustics of this beautiful space! See you there.
Source: Press Democrat

item.title: Marin Farmers Markets — Thu Dec 10, 8:00 AM — Marin Veterans' Memorial Auditorium
item.description:
Price: Free
Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market.
Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. The market takes place rain or shine.
www.aginstitutemarin.org
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Dem
